title: Video Footage Contradicts DHS Claims After ICE SUV Hits California Activist
snippet: Local police and video evidence have dismantled the Department of Homeland Security's claim that a Northern California man 'jumped on the hood' of an ICE vehicle, triggering a criminal investigation into the incident.
content:
A local police department in Northern California has launched a criminal investigation into a collision involving an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) vehicle, citing video evidence that directly refutes federal claims that a pedestrian jumped onto the officer's SUV.

Antonio Moreida, 37, was monitoring federal immigration activity in Woodland, California, on Tuesday morning when he was hit by a black Chevy Tahoe driven by an ICE agent. Multiple video recordings—including footage from a nearby home surveillance camera, a bystander’s phone, and Moreida’s own GoPro—show the SUV striking Moreida as he stood in the street recording federal vehicles.

Federal Account Disproved by Video

Following the incident, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) initially claimed that Moreida was an "agitator" who jumped onto the hood of the vehicle and "flopped for the camera." However, Woodland Police Chief Ryan Kinnan publicly questioned the federal narrative after reviewing footage from the scene, calling DHS's official statement "inconsistent" with physical and visual evidence.

By Thursday, federal officials appeared to backtrack on their initial claims. In an updated statement, an ICE spokesperson no longer alleged that Moreida had jumped onto the car, instead arguing that he was standing in the middle of an active road and impeding law enforcement actions.

Local Backlash and Investigation

Legal experts and local officials have pushed back against the federal narrative. Ryan Schwank, a former ICE attorney and agency whistleblower, noted that video footage showed Moreida was well within his rights to document law enforcement activity and was not blocking the vehicle.

Woodland Mayor Tom Stallard condemned the false statements from DHS, promising a thorough and impartial local investigation. U.S. Representative Mike Thompson also called for an internal federal probe, criticizing ICE's history of misleading the public during high-profile enforcement operations.
